Notably this order also shows PARTIAL physical construction actually happened before the project died: 'Laying of 30 Km pipeline out of total 47 Km pipeline from Jaigarh to Hathkhamba' and '30 Km pipeline out of total 53 Km pipeline from Mangalore to Udupi' -- so this was not a paper-only proposal, real pipe went into the ground on two sub-sections before the whole 635-km project was killed. (2) APTEL Appeal No. 311 of 2022 (H-ENERGY PRIVATE LIMITED v. PNGRB, judgment pronounced 10.05.2023, aptel.gov.in/sites/default/files/Jud2023/A311of22_100523.pdf -- fetched via the working http:// scheme, pdftotext-confirmed) is H-Energy's OWN appeal against PNGRB's termination of the JMPL authorization. The single most important document is the sponsor's OWN regulatory filing: https://www.pngrb.gov.in/pdf/public-notice/EoI29092020.pdf, GSPL India Gasnet Limited's (GIGL) 17-Sep-2020 letter to PNGRB's Secretary, 'Submission of Expression of Interest (EOI) for Laying, Building and Operating Natural Gas Pipeline from Langtala (Jaisalmer District, Rajasthan) to Pachpadra (Barmer District, Rajasthan)', filed under PNGRB's NGPL Authorization Regulations 2008. This is a scanned/image PDF -- it 200s but has NO text layer at all (confirmed via both PyPDF2 and pdftotext, which both return empty strings for every page), so url_verifier's substring screen fails it on every token; I OCR'd all 11 pages myself (PyMuPDF render -> tesseract) and read the actual content directly, which is a stronger check than the automated screen, not a weaker one. The letter states verbatim: 'Focus Energy Limited is expecting production of 4 MMSCMD gas from its gas field in Langtala, Jaisalmer District. In order to connect the said gas source to the national gas grid... GIGL is hereby submitting Expression of Interest... The approximate length of the pipeline will be around 290 kms.' Schedule-A (page 3) gives Point of Origin = 'Langtala, Jaisalmer District, Rajasthan' and End Point = 'Pachpadra in Barmer District, Rajasthan'. Independently, PNGRB's own tender portal page (https://www.pngrb.gov.in/eng-web/ng-bid-16.html, url_verifier OK on 'Langtala'+'Pachpadra') lists 'Langtala - Pachpadra Natural Gas Pipeline (LPPL)', Tender Reference BID/NGPL/16/2020/01/LPPL/01 dated 27.11.2020, with a full corrigendum history (25.03.2021 through 26.04.2022) and finally 'Public Notice for Annulment of Bid No. BID/NGPL/16/2020/01/LPPL, Updated Date: 05.05.2022'. This is an inter-connector line tying a single new field into the national trunk grid, the same 'transmission not gathering' pattern found on the sibling Kakinada-Vizag-Srikakulam row (P0932) audited earlier in this batch. resolutions.researcher_notes: Starting from the sheet's own wiki citations (2 Business Standard articles + 1 Hindu BusinessLine article + 1 Economic Times article), all four resolve live and I read full text of each. EXISTENCE: unambiguous. In 2007-08 the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas authorized Relogistics Infrastructure Ltd (Relog), a subsidiary of Reliance Gas Transportation Infrastructure Ltd (RGTIL, 'a RIL group company' per Business Standard), to build four trunk gas pipelines totalling 2,175 km: Kakinada-Haldia, Kakinada-Chennai, Chennai-Tuticorin and Chennai-Bangalore-Mangalore. Kakinada-Haldia itself is independently and specifically named (not just swept into an aggregate figure) in three of the four citations: 'RIL firm may lose Kakinada-Haldia gas line project' (Business Standard, dateline Jan 21 2013) gives the route explicitly as 'the proposed 1,100-km pipeline from Kakinada in Andhra to Haldia in West Bengal'; 'Petroleum regulator wants Reliance Gas' pipeline licences cancelled' (Hindu BusinessLine, published 2012-06-05, verified via article:published_time meta tag) lists 'Kakinada-Haldia' by name among the four authorized RGTIL lines and describes PNGRB pushing for cancellation over a bank-guarantee/deadline dispute; 'RGTIL loses rights to lay gas pipelines' (Business Standard, dateline Jan 25 2013) confirms the government formally cancelled all four RGTIL authorizations, naming Kakinada-Haldia first in the list, citing RGTIL's own stated reason (falling KG-D6 output made the pipeline uneconomic). CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as a gas transmission trunk line -- explicitly called a 'trunk pipeline'/one of 'four trunk pipelines' in the sourcing, cross-state (Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal) at 1,100 km, not a gathering/feeder/CGD line. DUPLICATE CHECK against the roster's other 12 India-gas cancelled rows: none overlaps this corridor -- P0932 (Kakinada-Vizag-Srikakulam) runs north along the coast within Andhra Pradesh only, and P2752 (Kondalapalli-Tirupati) runs south; neither reaches West Bengal. Not a relabel of any other row. IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION NOTE (not a duplicate risk for P3342, but worth flagging for the record): the sheet's 4th wiki citation, an Economic Times article ('GAIL, ONGC to invest Rs 3,000 cr for pipeline project', dateline Feb 2 2007), describes a DIFFERENT, competing Kakinada-Haldia proposal -- a GAIL/ONGC 50-50 SPV building a 1,000-km pipeline via Peddapuram-Srikakulam-Bhubaneshwar-Cuttack-Kharagpur to Pandua near Kolkata, to move ONGC's own KG-DWN-98/2 gas, explicitly described in the same article as running 'almost parallel to a similar pipeline proposed by Reliance Industries.' P3342's Owner1=Reliance Industries Ltd (100%) confirms this GEM row tracks the RIL/RGTIL project, correctly, not the GAIL/ONGC one -- but the wiki page's own citation list conflates the two histories under one page, and I found no evidence the GAIL/ONGC SPV pipeline was ever separately built or tracked elsewhere in GEM. That is a scope question for a future Discovery pass on this corridor, not a P3342 defect.
